summary: A revised BBN schedule for adding core memory to IMPs and TIPs. Completed retrofits were removed and the CCA retrofit date moved from March 20 to February 28. It restates the text of RFC 434 and was itself replaced by RFC 476.

plainLanguage.summary: An updated calendar for upgrading memory in the network's boxes, crossing off finished ones and moving one date earlier.

subtitle: A schedule for upgrading the network's IMP and TIP memory

tldr.problem: The ARPANET's IMP and TIP computers needed more memory to handle growing network traffic.
tldr.mechanism: BBN scheduled a systematic retrofit across all network sites, coordinated with planned maintenance to minimize disruption.
tldr.outcome: The retrofits upgraded IMPs to 16K words and TIPs to 28K or 32K words, completed in phases during 1973.

today: RFC 447 is Historic and was replaced by RFC 476. It served its purpose as a scheduling document for a one-time hardware retrofit in early 1973.

sections.title: Memory Retrofit Program
sections.content:
In early 1973, BBN began retrofitting the IMP (Interface Message Processor) and TIP (Terminal Interface Processor) computers that routed traffic on the ARPANET. The goal was to give each machine more memory: IMPs would gain 16K words of core memory, and TIPs would gain 28K words (or 32K with the magnetic tape option).

The RFC is an update to RFC 434, announcing that completed retrofits had been removed from the schedule and one site's date had moved earlier.
sections.plainLanguage: The early network's computers needed a memory upgrade. This note updates which dates they were being swapped out.

sections.title: The Retrofit Schedule
sections.content:
The schedule coordinated with each site's regular monthly preventive maintenance to minimize user disruption, though machines would be down longer than usual during the retrofit. The retrofits ran from February through April 1973, touching about 18 major network sites.

Sites affected included universities (Stanford, MIT, Utah, UCLA), research centers (SRI, ISI, RAND), and government installations (Belvoir, NOAA). BBN asked sites anticipating floor space problems (since the TIP would expand to two cabinets) to contact Hawley Rising for assistance.
sections.plainLanguage: Each network site got a date when its computers would be upgraded. The work was scheduled during maintenance windows to avoid disrupting users too much.

sections.title: Status
sections.content: RFC 447 is Historic and was replaced by RFC 476. The retrofit program itself finished in 1973, and the memory expansions it described became standard for those machines for years afterward.
sections.plainLanguage: This was just a planning document for a 1973 hardware upgrade. The project finished long ago.

references.text: McKenzie, A., "IMP/TIP Memory Retrofit Schedule", RFC 434, December 1972.
